title: The sunnah as second
hookLine: the sunnah explains and details the Qur'an

lines: PRAY AS YOU HAVE SEEN ME PRAYING.
cards: A group of young men have spent some days with the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ, and now they're about to set off home to their people. The Qur'an gives them the command, in Pickthall's words: "Establish worship."
It gives it again and again. What it doesn't give is a step-by-step. When to stand, how to bow, what to say, how many units: the text leaves that out.
So before they go, in a report kept in Sahih al-Bukhari, the Prophet tells them how to teach the prayer. Pray as you have seen me praying. Today: the sunnah as second.

teach.b: First, what sunnah means here: the Prophet's way, what he said, did and approved, carried in the hadith of the last block. In fiqh it stands second, right after the Qur'an.
Second, the book points to it. The Qur'an says Allah sent the reminder down to the Prophet so that he would explain to people what had been sent down to them.
And it tells believers, in Pickthall's words, "Obey Allah, and obey the messenger." The second source isn't bolted on from outside; the first source names it. Third, how it explains.
Scholars describe the sunnah doing more than one job.
It details what the Qur'an gives in brief, like the prayer: pray as you have seen me praying.
It shows how a general command is carried out: the Qur'an commands the poor-due, and the sunnah sets out which wealth is due and how much. It confirms what the Qur'an already says.
And scholars discuss, and differ over, rulings found in the sunnah that the Qur'an doesn't mention. Fourth, who carries it.
Sunni schools receive the sunnah through the reports of the companions, weighed by the methods of the last block.

Shia scholars receive it also through the Imams of the Prophet's family, whose words and example they hold to be part of it, weighed through their own collections. Both put the sunnah right after the book.
That's why the hadith block came first: the second source rests on knowing which reports are sound.

how: Muslims learn the details of prayer, charity and fasting from the sunnah, by watching parents and teachers pray and by studying the hadith and the fiqh built on them.

games.q: what does “the sunnah as second” mean?
o: an optional extra prayer, separate from the law
a later custom added to Islam after the Prophet's time
the Prophet's way, standing after the Qur'an and explaining it

games.q: the sunnah as second — tap the pairs.
p: pray as you have seen me praying
a channel of sunnah for Shia scholars

s: the Qur'an spells out every movement of the prayer
it commands prayer and speaks of bowing and prostrating; the details come from the sunnah.
"pray as you have seen me praying" is in Sahih al-Bukhari
said to young men about to go home and teach their people.
Shia scholars don't use the sunnah
they receive it through the Prophet's reports and also through the Imams of his family.

games.q: you're one of the young men who stayed with the Prophet, and now you're heading home to teach your people. how will you teach them to pray?
o: read them the verses that command prayer and let them work out the rest.
pray the way you saw him pray, and teach them that.
design a form that suits your town.
games.why: he told them: pray as you have seen me praying. the sunnah filled in what the command gave in brief.

practice: Picture a prayer you've seen or prayed: standing, then bowing, then the forehead resting on the ground.
The Qur'an speaks of bowing and prostrating; the shape of those movements, one after another, comes from people watching the Prophet pray and doing what they saw.
Picture them slowly, in order, then come back to your own body, your hands, your breath.
